messages:
pagerduty-bot: 🔔 ALERT: High 5xx and routing errors observed on inference endpoints. Error spike originates from routing-controller in us-west-2; "capacity_tier" tag evaluation failing for several tenant ids. 40% error rate, affected: dedicated pool overlap. Paging dev-oncall.
Ashley: oncall here, seeing a bunch of gateway errors + model-mismatch logs. grabbing `routing-controller` logs now.
Devon: pulling policy snapshot from /etc/routing/policies/current.json — looks like a newly deployed policy change 15m ago.
Sam: I see an odd rule: `if reserved == false then prefer: dedicated` — that seems reversed for the flagged tenants. Could be the cause of hosted->dedicated spillover.
Marta: Confirmed: several tenants were supposed to be pinned to Dedicated but the policy predicates evaluate to false because tag parsing failed (regex bug).
Daniel: Workaround idea: disable the fallback path from hosted->dedicated temporarily so hosted traffic stays on hosted while we patch. Rolling a feature-flag: `routing.disable_dedicated_fallback = true`.
Ashley: Doing the flag toggle now. Command: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/flags/routing/disable_dedicated_fallback -d '{"value":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY'`
incidents-bot: ACTION — Feature flag set by Ashley. Now: routing fallback disabled.
Sam: After the flag flip, 5xx rate dropping to ~7% and latency for affected endpoints back to baseline. Good call.
Devon: Root cause: policy DSL produced by recent PR #782 added an OR clause which changed evaluation order. Example snippet from deployed policy:
```
- match: tenant.metadata.reserved == "false" || tenant.labels.beta == "true"
  prefer: dedicated
```
The OR short-circuits and matches unintended tenants. Unit tests didn't cover label parsing case.
Marta: Ok patch incoming to routing-controller to change to explicit equality checks and add safe parsing. Draft diff attached.
Daniel: Also need an immediate remediation for tenant isolation — marking the 5 affected tenants as reserved= true in the metadata store to ensure they don't get misrouted. I'll run the update.
Ashley: Doing metadata patch: `for t in [cust-17,cust-88,cust-413]; do api update /tenants/$t --set reserved=true; done` — updating now.
incidents-bot: NOTE — metadata updates applied by Ashley.
Sam: Monitoring: errors down to 1.2%, all dedicated pool saturation metrics normal.
Devon: Deploying routing-controller patch (hotfix) with corrected predicate evaluation and added unit tests. Will deploy to canary first.
Marta: Canary looks clean for 10 minutes. Rolling to prod in waves.
Daniel: After full rollout, enabling fallback again and validating policy behavior.
Ashley: Re-enable fallback: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/flags/routing/disable_dedicated_fallback -d '{"value":false}'` — done.
incidents-bot: ACTION — fallback re-enabled. Post-change check in progress.
Sam: Post-fix checks: no more misrouted tenants, error rate stable, latency normal.
Devon: Customer impact: 5 tenants experienced degraded availability between ~T+00:05 and T+00:26. No data loss, requests retried by client SDKs. Notified affected account owners via support.
Marta: Follow-ups: 1) Add predicate evaluation unit tests for policy DSL 2) Add CI gate that runs a small tenant-tag emulation before policy rollouts 3) Add alert for sudden change in ded/hosted traffic ratio per-tenant.
Daniel: Also propose an emergency knob in routing-controller to pin-by-tenant until the policy is validated (short TTL).
Ashley: Handoff: I'll document timeline and put postmortem draft in #postmortems. Sam, you're on next oncall for 08:00 UTC — handing over.
Sam: Thanks — I have the runbook and logs. I'll watch the metrics for 2 hours.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: routing-controller policy regression causing capacity-tier misrouting. Severity: P2. Root cause: predicate parsing/ordering bug in policy DSL. Mitigation: feature-flag rollback, tenant metadata patch, hotfix to routing-controller, re-enable fallback.
Marta: TL;DR for postmortem: bad OR short-circuit in policy + missing unit tests -> dedicated spillover -> 5 affected tenants degraded.
Devon: Adding owners: @Marta (routing-controller), @Devon (policy DSL), @Daniel (metadata/ops).
Ashley: I'll start the postmortem with a timeline and customer impact section. Assigned action items to owners.
Sam: :white_check_mark: Closing thread after postmortem created.
